display.title: Yud-Beis Tammuz: The Day the Frierdiker Rebbe Was Freed
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Tammuz, Uncle Yossi explains why Yud-Beis Tammuz, when the Frierdiker Rebbe was freed from prison in Russia, is a day of joy and good resolutions.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz. Uncle Yossi notes that the month of Tammuz has both sad and happy days, and, following Shlomo HaMelech's 'there is a time for everything', he speaks about the happy one. On the twelfth of Tammuz in 1927, the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, was freed from prison in Russia, where he had been jailed for teaching Torah to Jewish children. Hashem saved him through many miracles, and he was released on his own birthday. His freedom was a redemption for all Jews: he went on to build a network of yeshivos around the world so that children everywhere could learn Torah in purity. Uncle Yossi reminds listeners how fortunate they are to live where Torah may be learned freely, and asks every Tzivos Hashem soldier to mark the day with joy and a resolution to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos.
display.lesson: Celebrate Yud-Beis Tammuz by resolving to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos, the ideals the Frierdiker Rebbe risked his life for.

date.note: 'Today is the first day of the new month... Aleph Tammuz'; Rosh Chodesh Monday and Tuesday.

advisories.note: The Frierdiker Rebbe was imprisoned in Russia, his life in danger, for teaching Torah.

sources_cited.note: 'Eis lakol', there is a time for everything, cited from Shlomo HaMelech.
